correctness.rationale: For [x,y]=z central over char!=2, each genuine half-derivation is D_B,ell(u,t)=(B u,ell(u)+(tr B)t/2), with B arbitrary 2x2 and ell a linear form. Two-locality on (w,λw) gives degree-one homogeneity; on (u,s),(u,t) forces quotient g(u) independent of t. In converse, for independent u,v choose B fixed by g on a basis and ell to interpolate h; for collinear nonzero projected vectors choose B with arbitrary prescribed trace and map on one vector, then ell, with the center-only and proportional cases handled separately. Over finite F_q homogeneous functions are independent on projective directions, giving q^(2(q+1)+(q²+q+1))=q^(q²+3q+3); linear two-local maps q^7, genuine half derivations q^6. Independent mod3 Gaussian elimination solved all 1890 unordered point-pair interpolation equations for five randomly generated homogeneous maps; projective counts checked at q=3,5,7. Finite tests are corroboration, not the universal proof.
